A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GCA framework and contain 13 readable pages, including equations, figures, tables and Appendix A.1. Corresponding content can be reliably matched; pages 3–10 and 13 are identical in text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original fine-tuning and tool-use evaluations, including error rates in Table 2 and benchmark accuracies in Table 3.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original empirical evaluations and results in Tables 2–3, including GCA's end-to-end answer accuracy of 88.2.

M1.justification: The data-curation pipeline, Qwen2.5-VL 7B LoRA adaptation, tool interfaces and agent control procedure remain unchanged in Sections 3–5 and Appendix A.1.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation retain the same textual and visual-temporal data and climate tool-use tasks. The six countries explicitly named in v3's introduction were already specified in v1's dataset description and city inventory.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain the same comparators: GPT-5, Claude 4.5 Sonnet, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Qwen2.5-VL 7B and Pixtral-12B.

E3.justification: Both versions retain the 91-question benchmark, preprocessing, fine-tuning settings, shared prompting and tool schemas, and step-by-step and end-to-end evaluation modes and metrics.

E4.justification: The tool-error breakdown in Table 2 and fine-tuning comparisons and execution-behavior analyses in Section 5.3 are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both describe a single fine-tuning run and report point estimates without repeated-seed summaries, confidence intervals or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: No result entries or findings change. Table 3 retains GCA's ToolAcc of 94.2, AnsAcc of 88.2 and AnsAcc+I of 89.1; Table 2 retains its error rates of 12.7%, 8.3% and 3.9%. Dataset counts and illustrated examples also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(3), covering keyword filtering, spatial matching and temporal windows, and the formal agent-trajectory description are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: Both claim a roughly 200k-item regional multimodal dataset, a tool-augmented climate agent and improved reliability through fine-tuning and tool integration. The GCC wording clarifies the geographical focus already explicit in v1's data description.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 retains the explanation linking accuracy gains to improved tool execution and schema adherence. Section 7 retains the same limitations concerning partial validation, tool dependence, benchmark coverage and deployment oversight.

D1.justification: Data-processing instructions, Section 5.1 hyperparameters and Appendix A.1 tool specifications remain identical. No implementation details or code/data access instructions are added or revised.

R1.justification: MMClima changes from Anonymous Authors (2026) to Sheikh et al. (2025), but its title and link identify the same work. This bibliographic update leaves the cited-work set and substantive research positioning unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized edits introduce GCC terminology in the title and abstract, explicitly enumerate six countries in the introduction, add an author email and update MMClima's citation metadata. Section organization and the remaining narrative are unchanged.

P2.justification: The title and author block are reformatted, and reference reordering causes limited reflow, including movement of the appendix headings within page 12. Figures 1–4 and Tables 1–4 retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: V3 states the existing six-country focus more explicitly in the opening and replaces MMClima's anonymous attribution with named authors and a 2025 date consistent with Table 1. These modestly improve clarity and reference consistency; methods, empirical support, reproducibility details and limitations remain unchanged.
